# Sikkhānisaṁsa Sutta (Iti 46 (It 2.19 PTS It 40))

**ID:** Iti 46 (It 2.19 PTS It 40)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Sikkhānisaṁsa Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sikkhānisaṁsa Sutta* ("The Benefits of Training") is the 46th discourse of the *Itivuttaka* (found in the Dukanipāta at It 2.19, PTS p. 40) [Windisch 1889]. In this sutta, the Buddha instructs the mendicants to dwell having the training as their benefit (*sikkhānisaṁsā*), wisdom/discernment as supreme (*paññuttarā*), release as their essence (*vimuttisārā*), and mindfulness as their governing principle (*satādhipateyyā*) [Windisch 1889]. For those practicing in this manner, one of two fruits is to be expected: final knowledge in this very life (*diṭṭhe va dhamme aññā*) or, if there is a remainder of clinging, non-return (*anāgāmitā*) [Windisch 1889].

Full parallels are preserved in Chinese within the *Itivuttaka* translation (T 765.91) and the *Saṁyuktāgama* (SA 825). In addition, passage-level parallels to its verse material occur across several versions of the *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* traditions, including T 210.1, T 212.1, T 213.1, the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G3-Dhp 51–60), and the Sanskrit and Tibetan Udānavarga (UV 1 and Uv Kg 1).
